newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Japanese join Votorantim to bid for Brazil CVRD.
newsitem.headline: Japanese join Votorantim to bid for Brazil CVRD.

text.p: A group of Japanese companies led by steelmaker Nippon Steel Corp has decided to join the consortium led by Brazil's Votorantim to participate in the privatization auction of Brazilian state mining giant CVRD, a local news agency said.
The group of Japanese companies consists of 12 firms led by Nippon Steel and trading company Nissho Iwai Corp, Invest News said.
It said the Japanese companies, most of them steelmakers, yet had to decide on the size of their stake in the consortium, probably between 10 and 15 percent.
The Japanese are not interested in managing CVRD, but want to guard against control of the firm being used against them by others, Invest News said.

The Japanese opted for Votorantim's consortium, which is also expected to include South Africa's Anglo American Corp, because Votorantim would actively manage CVRD if it emerges as the winning bidder at the auction, Invest News said.
A 45 percent voting stake in CVRD will be auctioned April 29 on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange for a minimum price of 3 billion reais ($2.83 billion).
((-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
